name: Singapore Airlines style
touchpoints: the annual report, monthly operating statistics, seat maps and the app's boarding pass

sample.topic: Monthly operating statistics of Vizney Air, a fictional long-haul airline with one hub at Chicago O'Hare (ORD): 14 routes in five route regions, one 247-seat layout (Business J 28 · Premium Economy S 21 · Economy Y 198), October 2026 of FY2026/27, against plan and October 2025. US dollars; flights, passengers and seat-km count both directions, on-time departures count Chicago only

devices.boardingPass: KPI row: a white pass with a 1px #c8d6f1 frame and an 8px radius. A navy #00266b band (MONTHLY OPERATING STATISTICS · FY2026/27 · MONTH 7 OF 12, 11px/600 caps, 0.14em) → a FROM ORD → TO <route region> line (airport codes in the display face 32px/600 navy, the destinations as mono codes) with FLIGHTS and SEATS FLOWN at the right → five fields in a subgrid (caps label 11px/600 #666 → value 34px/600 with a 15px unit → vs plan → vs last year) → where the barcode sits, passengers by day (one bar a day, the busiest day teal #0096ae, the rest #868ba0). The navy stub on the right holds the load factor at 52px (the seat number's place), two chips (vs plan, vs last year; success #03760b on #cdf0cf, error #dc0202 on #fff1f0) and the breakeven load factor with its margin at the bottom
devices.seatMap: Figure 1, cabin load: the 247-seat layout laid on its side (Business 1-2-1 rows 11–18 without 13, Premium Economy 2-3-2 rows 21–23, Economy 3-3-3 rows 31–52), cabin bands in the cabin colours with code and seat count ('J · 28'), row numbers above, seat letters at the left (A B C · D E G · H J K), the forward zone as a light green band behind the first five Economy rows with its own load factor. An average flight's sold seats are filled window and aisle first: the cabin the title names in teal, the others gray #afafaf, empty seats white with a #a6b4cd outline. Below, a strip of three cabins (cabin-colour top rule → name and code → load factor → x of n seats sold · y empty → vs plan). No fuselage outline, windows or seat icons. Under 420px the map stacks: J and S above, Y below
devices.operatingStatistics: Headline and Table 1, from the monthly operating statistics release and the annual report's OPERATING STATISTICS table: the lead sentence states the result ('Traffic rose 10.9% year-on-year on 9.7% more capacity, and the load factor came in at 86.5%, 0.8 pts above plan.'), then a navy head band with white caps and units in parentheses ((thousand), (million), (%), (pts), (¢/pkm)), route-region group rows on #e5e9f0 with subtotals, the Systemwide row bold under a 2px navy rule, changes in a separate sign column ('+ 2.3', '− 3.2'), 'n.m.' for a route with no last year, bad values (below plan, below the 85% on-time target) in #dc0202 with their sign

parts.bookingWidget: The screen frame comes from singaporeair.com's booking widget: the route-region filter is the navy tab bar (12px/600 caps, 0.125em), the chosen tab white with only its top-left corner rounded 16px, and the white panel below it with 16px bottom corners holds the headline, the lead and the boarding pass. A 1px orange separator (8px tall) sits between header items
parts.hairline: Orange #ff9f00 is a hairline, never data: a 3px bar left of the headline and every section title (the site's .left-border titles) and the 3px underline of the active code tab
parts.routeBoard: Figure 3, routes against breakeven: one row per route, lowest margin first; city name and mono airport code, a bar from the breakeven line (the zero, a 1px #222222 rule) in pts on a fixed −4 to +14 scale, red #dc0202 with the value on its left below breakeven, gray #afafaf above; PLF and BLF columns at the right. Rows stretch (25–44px) so the card ends level with Figure 4
parts.hubBank: Figure 4, departures from Chicago by hour: one bar per scheduled hour, on time gray #afafaf and late red #dc0202 on top with a 2px gap, the evening bank 17:00–20:59 as a #edf4ff band labelled with its own on-time rate, 'flights' above the axis, hours 00–21 with the bank hours bold
parts.annualReportChart: Figure 2 and every axis use the annual report's chart grammar: the unit above the axis ('%', 'flights'), no gridlines, a #a6b4cd base line and ticks, the latest period bold, uppercase gold figure labels (FIGURE 2 · LOAD FACTOR BY MONTH), notes numbered like the release ('Note 1:')

validation.tool: dataviz validate_palette.js (OKLab), mode light, on the card #ffffff
validation.categorical: From the annual report's charts: bars in teal #0096ae, a second series in deep blue #005584 (also its table heads), bronze #c3892a as the third. All pairs pass: lightness inside 0.43–0.77, chroma ≥ 0.1, CVD ΔE 17.3 (bronze–teal, protan), normal vision 19.5 (deep blue–teal), contrast 3.52, 7.98 and 3.03:1. The site's navy #00266b and orange #ff9f00 stay on frames and hairlines
validation.cabins: The cabin colours #12447d · #4f635f · #084935 fail as data (lightness under 0.43, chroma under 0.1, normal-vision 12.9), so they only band the seat map, always with the code and seat count in white (9.77, 6.40 and 10.42:1)
validation.other: #afafaf (darkGrey) is neutral by design: the lightness band and chroma floor do not apply; at 2.19:1 it always has a second cue (value labels, the 2px gap between stacked segments, a table)
validation.comparison: #868ba0 (the annual report's cool gray) for plan: 3.38:1, always dashed (6 4) and labelled at its end. Last year #c4c9d4 sits behind both, solid and labelled at its end in #666666
validation.sequential: one teal hue around the subject (#74bfcc → #004a59): monotone lightness, every gap ≥ 0.06, light end 2.09:1, hue spread 8°
validation.diverging: bronze arm #d9ab62 → #8a5a14 (light end 2.11:1, hue spread 7°) and teal arm #74bfcc → #006a7f (2.09:1, 8°) pass the ordinal checks; poles CVD 14.4 (protan), normal 18.3; the midpoint is lightGrey #dddddd
validation.status: good #03760b (5.83:1) and bad #dc0202 (5.18:1) from the site's alerts; between them CVD 8.9 (protan), normal 33.9. Status is never colour alone: a change keeps its arrow, sign and comparison words
validation.text: label steps: teal #00788c 5.17:1, bronze #946e31 4.63:1; ink #222222 15.9:1, secondary #666666 5.74:1 on white; the orange hairline is 2.06:1 on white, so it never carries text
validation.plan: Each figure has one subject: Figure 1 the cabin the title names (teal) against gray cabins, Figure 2 the actual load factor against a dashed plan and a pale last year, Figure 3 only the routes below breakeven in red, Figure 4 only the late departures in red, the pass barcode only the busiest day in teal

code.note: a white code pane; the screen's own text steps (navy keyword, green string, orange number, gold function), all at 4.5:1 or more on white

sans.role: body, labels, values in tables and charts. Figtree stands in for Proxima Nova (the site's --font-primary): set in the same string at 20px Proxima runs 437.5px with a 0.714 x/cap ratio, Figtree 447.7px with 0.714. singaporeair.com/ko_KR loads no Hangul web font, so Korean uses Pretendard for everything

display.role: headings, airport codes and big values. Stands in for the site's own heading face (a humanist sans with a binocular g): in the same 24px string it runs 424.7px, Source Sans 3 439.1px, also with a binocular g. Headings stay at 400 like the site's h2; values at 600

mono.role: airport and route codes, file names and code; Hangul in code comments falls back to Pretendard

layout.header: 84px white header + 56px navy tab bar, then the white widget panel joined to the chosen tab
rows: white header: VIZNEY AIR caps eyebrow and Operating Statistics (display 30px/400 navy); period, the EN/KO pill, Export PDF (outlined), Copy as Markdown (navy)

navy tab bar: Systemwide 14 · The Americas 3 · Europe 4 · East Asia 3 · South West Pacific 2 · West Asia and Africa 2, with the month and comparison at the right behind an orange separator (from 1360px)
the widget panel: headline with the orange bar, the lead paragraph, the boarding pass (main + 270px stub), 'Note 1'
Load: cabins and the year: Figure 1 seat map · Figure 2 load factor by month (its plot takes the extra height so both cards end on one line)
Routes and the Chicago hub: Figure 3 routes against breakeven · Figure 4 departures by hour (its plot takes the extra height)
Operating statistics: Table 1, the full width
How it's built: intro, three steps, the window (package 240px · figure and checks · code)

footer: VIZNEY STYLES · 05 catalog line, sample note, notice, back link

measured.widget: booking tabs: active tab white, radius 16px 0 0 0, 12px/700 caps 1.5px navy; inactive 12px/600 white; segmented pill radius 40px; SEARCH button #00266b, 12px/600 caps 1.44px, height 48, radius 4px; titles .left-border 3px #ff9f00 with 15px padding; h2 24px/400 navy
measured.cabins: --cabin colours: business #053a76 · #12447d · #2a578a, premium economy #495b57 · #4f635f · #5b6f6b, economy #053c2a · #084935 · #12533f · #1c5d49 (the middle 'standard' steps are used)
measured.ir: Monthly operating statistics: a lead sentence with the result (passenger traffic up x% year-on-year), tables of available seat-km (million), revenue passenger-km (million), passengers carried (thousand), passenger load factor (%), load factor by route region (East Asia · The Americas · Europe · South West Pacific · West Asia and Africa); changes as % and pts; 'Note 1:' footnotes
measured.annualReport: OPERATING STATISTICS table: navy head band, light-blue group rows, units in parentheses, a separate sign column, 'n.m.', passenger breakeven load factor; charts: uppercase amber titles, the unit above the axis, no gridlines, the latest year bold, teal #0096ae bars, deep blue #005584 and bronze #c3892a second series, cool gray #868ba0
measured.touchpoints: Seat map PDFs: cabin headers 'Business Class - J / n seats', seat letters A B C – D E G – H J K, row 13 skipped, a light green FORWARD ZONE band; the app's digital boarding pass: a navy header band over a white body of labelled fields (photos viewed only, not used; the real seat counts are not reused)
measured.fonts: --font-primary Proxima Nova (400/600/700, tabular figures); headings in the site's own humanist sans; ko_KR loads no Hangul web font
